questions.help:
OTHER FACTORS    
   
25 Clothing  
25.1 The clothing of motorcyclist
A motorcycle does not provide the rider with a secure and protective shell. This makes the rider vulnerable in road traffic collisions; to the elements, such as, in the cold, wind, rain, and so on. The body of the rider and any passenger realises the force of all of these external elements, the weather and any possible impact. It is therefore absolutely essential to use a dress code that adequately protects them all of the time regardless of the time of year.
The motorcyclist’s outfit has to be colourful and eye-catching, and should be made of leather or other similar material. It should have contrasting colours and design, with reflective bands that allow it to be distinguished from a distance.
A ‘set of leathers’ (a leather jacket and trousers) is advocated, as it will:
Does not flap with the air.
Protects against the wind during the trip.
Provide protection from possible damage, scrapes and consequent rubbing or contact sores to the rider. In the event of falling off abrasive wounds are minimised.
(Página 50 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
Road traffic collisions  
   
1 A public health problem
Moreover, in addition to the human drama, it is important to highlight the enormous economic impact (either directly or indirectly) that occurs as a result of a traffic collision.
Costs derived from road traffic accidents are classified as human, material, healthcare and administrative.
Human costs include the loss of lives, productive capacity and physical and psychological suffering. Material costs consist of damages caused on vehicles and their loads as well as on the road and the environment. Healthcare costs comprise first aid, care and treatment of the wounded, rehabilitation and adaptations. Administrative costs hold those of police officers and firefighters and insurance and services management.
People believe that an accident has little effect on them but the cost is borne by taxpayers. The cost of vehicle insurance is also affected, as premiums are affected by collision data and the cost of accidents.
For these reasons, various international organisations, including the World Health Organisation (WHO), believe that road collisions are a priority public health problem throughout the world.
There is a serious need to work together to reduce the high numbers of dead and seriously injured on the roads.
(Página 248 del manual 'Learning to drive')

1.1 Basics
Inappropriate speed: This is driving at a speed not suited to the circumstances such as, the weather conditions, the circumstances of the road, traffic, the vehicle or the condition of the driver. The speed may be inappropriate but is within the permitted limits.
Appropriate speed: This is the adoption of an adequate speed which, while respecting the maximum and minimum limits, is suited to the changing traffic conditions, the road, the vehicle or the state of the driver. The appropriate speed allows the driver (and vehicle) to react to any obstacle or unexpected hazard that may occur.
(Página 170 del manual 'Learning to drive')

El tiempo desde que ve un peligro hasta que actúa, ¿cómo se llama?
What is the time from when you see a hazard until you act called?

answers.text:
Tiempo de frenado.
Braking time.

Tiempo de detención.
Stopping time.

Tiempo de reacción.
Reaction time.

questions.help:
Physical condition of the driver    
 
4 Reaction time
The reaction time is defined as the time that passes from when a driver sees a hazard (for example an obstacle etc; or hears a noise) until he responds to it.
The reaction time is not constant, although under normal conditions, it is approximately 0,75 second.
(Página 32 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.question:
Cuando el semáforo se ponga verde, ¿qué debe hacer?
When the traffic light turns green, what should you do?

answers.text:
Obedecer al semáforo, que tiene prioridad sobre la señal de stop.
Obey the traffic light, which has priority over the stop sign.

Obedecer al semáforo, pero debo ceder el paso.
Obey the traffic light, but I must give way to other traffic.

Obedecer la señal de stop.
Obey the stop sign.
